title: Claim
description: One sourced value for one field of one vehicle. Every number in the charts and CSVs traces back to a claim.

field.description: Dot-path into the vehicle schema, e.g. 'battery.pack_kwh' or 'charging.peak_dc_kw'

value.description: The claimed value, any JSON type. Default units are defined in vehicle-fields.md.

unit.description: Optional explicit unit override if it differs from the field default (e.g. 'lb-ft' vs 'Nm').

tier.description: P = primary (OEM spec sheet or press kit, EPA, NHTSA, DOE/Argonne, USPTO, government filing). S = secondary (outlet, teardown report, spec aggregator). D = derived from other claims; requires derivation. unverified = plausible but unconfirmed; flag it wherever it's shown.

source_name.description: Human-readable source, e.g. 'Lucid Motors Air Pure Technical Specifications (MY2025 PDF)'

source_url.description: Required for tier P and S. Omit only for tier D or unverified.

access_date.description: ISO date the claim was captured. Required on every claim so staleness is visible.

model_year.description: Model year of the source, if it differs from the vehicle's (e.g. a MY2025 spec sheet cited for a MY2026 vehicle).

disclosed_by_oem.description: True if the OEM published this value, even when it's cited through a secondary report (tier S). False or absent: the value comes from third-party testing or our own inference.

confidence.description: Subjective reliability, separate from tier. A single teardown report might be tier S, confidence medium.

conflicts_with.description: Ids (vehicle_id#field#source_name) of claims that disagree with this one. Both claims are kept and the conflict is flagged in the output.

inputs.description: Field paths used as inputs; use vehicle_id#field for another vehicle's claim.

assumptions.description: Assumptions built into the formula, e.g. 'assumes pack_kwh is usable, not gross'

uncertainty.description: Interval or stated error for derived or inferred values.

method.description: e.g. 'Monte Carlo, 10000 draws' or 'EPA 0.7x adjustment-factor bound'

notes.description: Caveats, what couldn't be confirmed, why a value looks odd.
